recovery.activation: Browser configuration refreshed; matching adapter installed with CLI override absent, ordinary-chat scope, restart and native hook trust required. Catalog published 24 models including six Web models. Previous managed generations retained for rollback.
recovery.rollbackScope: The proven current adapter generation and current-runtime manifest remain intact. Supported adapter rollback restores the original stock-Codex launch selection. Retained older managed artifacts are protected recovery material, but their removed external runtime paths prevent directly launching those old generations without rebinding to valid current anchors.
recovery.liveVerification: After normal Codex restart, the current adapter started against the updated official Node REPL. The first Web request hit the intentional configuration-reload guard before Send. A guarded Router restart loaded the changed configuration; the retry completed one native fixture read with exit code 0, exact paired output and recall of the original saved-chat marker. A fresh Stop test then confirmed cancellation with the same tab retained, followed by successful original-marker recall in that same chat, tab and binding.
recovery.configurationReload: Saved browser/tunnel changes require Router restart as well as Codex adapter restart. Updated the setup CLI hint and maintained setup instructions to include the existing guarded restart.
recovery.restartCliObservation: The service reported running and fresh health was ready, but its CLI aborted during Node shutdown with the Windows async-handle assertion. The service restart itself succeeded. Replaced forced CLI process.exit with process.exitCode, matching the existing start.mjs owner. The existing direct/control fixture now verifies natural event-loop drain across success, returned errors and ownership refusal; it fails with the previous implementation. No second live restart was used to try to reproduce the native assertion.
